text: The Ludwig Mond Award is presented annually by the Royal Society of Chemistry to recognize outstanding research in any area of inorganic chemistry. The recipient receives a £2000 monetary prize, a medal, and a certificate, and is required to complete a UK lecture tour. The winner is selected by the Dalton Division Awards Committee. In 2020, the Ludwig Mond Award was merged with the Nyholm Prize for Inorganic Chemistry to create the Mond-Nyholm Prize for Inorganic Chemistry. The award was established in 1981 to honor the life and contributions of chemist Dr Ludwig Mond, whose work was supported by an endowment from Imperial Chemical Industries (ICI). Dr Mond was born in Kassel, Germany in 1839 and became a prominent chemist and industrialist who later acquired British nationality.
